title: Metrics surface
preamble:
# Metrics surface

The engine's observable counters, gauges, and
histograms, delivered through a **typed integrator
callback** the engine invokes at
observable-event sites. Each emission is a
`ds_metric_t` value passed to the callback at emit
time; the integrator decides where it goes
(Prometheus / StatsD / Loki / OpenTelemetry / a
custom control-plane message / nowhere) inside
their callback body.

The engine's responsibility ends at calling the
callback with a well-formed `ds_metric_t`. No internal
buffering, no flush cadence, no transport choice, no
aggregation policy baked in. The integrator owns where
the data goes and at what cadence it arrives downstream.

## What this is not

- Not a transport spec. Prometheus format, StatsD,
  OpenTelemetry — integrator choices made inside
  the callback.
- Not a flush-cadence spec. Each metric is emitted
  once at its observable-event site; the integrator's
  callback decides when (or whether) to push the
  value onward.
- Not a rate-calculation spec. Counters are emitted
  monotonically; the integrator computes deltas /
  rates as their backend requires.
- Not a dashboards / alerting / SLO spec. Operator
  territory.
- Not a rule-author-visible surface. Rules don't
  write custom metrics; they store facts in the facts
  plane through the storage service.
